clue.text: Turn and punch, producing shower of blows

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a handle or key
to sock someone is to punch them

explanation.surface: A boxer twists and lands a punch, unleashing a flurry of blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower of blows' looks like a boxing flurry, but read 'shower' as 'one who shows': the thing that shows which way the wind blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A windsock is the airfield cone that indicates the direction a breeze is coming from, so it shows what blows.

clue.text: Comedian doting about his twin town in Australia

parts.note: a wag is a joker or comic person

indicators.note: the besotted word goes round the second comic

parts.note: gaga means besotted or infatuated
the comedian's twin is another of the same, a second wag

explanation.surface: A fond comic dotes on his twin who lives in an Australian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His twin' means another comedian just like the first, which is why the Australian town's name doubles itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagga Wagga is an inland city in New South Wales.

clue.text: She turns up in some — and same — order

indicators.text: turns up in some — and same — order
indicators.note: the word reads identically when turned up the grid, so its order is the same whichever way it runs

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman of a religious order turns up in the same order as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' does double duty in spirit: the letters are in the same order either way, and a nun belongs to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a female member of a religious community, so the answer is a woman.

clue.text: Nervous about hooter going around one, loudly

indicators.note: the timid word wraps round the bird and its contents

parts.note: shy means timid or nervous

indicators.note: the bird surrounds the letter for one

parts.note: an owl hoots, so it is a hooter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone jittery about a car horn sounding near a person, very loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a car horn or a nose; here it is the owl.
explanation.definitionFit: Showily means in a flashy, ostentatious way, which is one sense of loudly, as in loud clothes.

clue.text: Be leaving to start work as harvester in fall

indicators.note: the word be departs from the front of the phrase

parts.note: to become a cropper is to take up work as one who cuts crops
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quits to take a job harvesting crops in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' is not a verb here but letters to remove; 'fall' looks like autumn but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is a British idiom meaning to take a heavy tumble or fail badly.

clue.text: A street light on the wrong road

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A lone streetlamp shines over a traveller who has taken a wrong turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered off its proper route, which is being on the wrong road.

clue.text: Close around noon, say, in the country

indicators.note: the closing word goes round the noon and say letters

parts.note: to seal is to close up
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A deal is closed around midday, as it were, somewhere in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African nation, so it is a country.

clue.text: Minister agrees reforms after sign of hesitation, backing facility for drivers

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the hesitation sound

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister
er is the sound made when hesitating

indicators.note: the letters of agrees are re-formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A clergyman hesitates, then agrees to reforms, supporting provision for motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' tempts as a reversal signal, but it belongs to the definition: the gear used for driving backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverse gear lets a driver move a car backwards.

clue.text: Cry once you fall in second half

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: only the latter half of the word fall is used

explanation.surface: A shout goes up when you tumble after half-time.
explanation.definitionFit: A yell is a loud shout, so it is a cry.

clue.text: Weapons stores near castles in sticks

indicators.note: the near-and-castles letters sit inside the word for sticks

parts.note: gums are glues, things that stick
in chess notation castling on the king's side is written O-O

explanation.surface: Armouries are found near fortifications out in the remote countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' is the countryside (the boondocks) on the surface, but it is a verb-turned-noun for adhesives, GUMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunroom is a room where firearms are kept, so these are places for storing guns.

clue.text: Reportedly polite to conceal new moan

indicators.note: the sound-alike word wraps round the letter for new
signals that the word for polite is taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: civil means courteous or polite

explanation.surface: Someone, so we hear, is too well-mannered to hide a fresh complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: CIVIL said aloud is 'sivel'; 'to conceal' puts N inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to whine or whimper tearfully, a weak complaining cry.

clue.text: This hard, bare ground makes little difference

indicators.note: the three words are ground down and their letters re-formed

explanation.surface: Hard, bare soil makes little difference to the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairsbreadth is a tiny margin, a very small distance or gap.

clue.text: Carol first of all means to enter a mile heat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word all is used

parts.note: a way in is an entrance, a means of entering
heat can mean anger or passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: An instruction for a race: the ways to get into a one-mile heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' and 'enter' look like separate words but together make WAY IN; 'heat' is temper, not a race.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a well-known Christmas carol about the infant Jesus in a stable.

clue.text: Relatives and friends made scapegoats

parts.note: aunts are relatives
allies are friends or supporters

explanation.surface: Family and friends have been made the ones to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: An AUNT SALLY is a British fairground or pub game where sticks are thrown at a dummy's head, hence a target of easy blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sallies are figures set up to be attacked or blamed, which is what scapegoats are.

clue.text: Missing rockets, perhaps, like hard landing?

definitions.meaning: to carpet someone is to give them a rocket, a sharp telling-off, so this means escaping a reprimand
a staircase landing with bare boards and no floor covering is hard underfoot

explanation.definitionFit: Not carpeted means both not reprimanded and having a bare floor, as on a hard landing.

clue.text: Pa has no time to eat

indicators.note: the letter for time is removed from the word for the system

parts.note: PA is a public address system, and Tannoy is a British brand name for one

explanation.surface: Dad is too busy to sit down for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pa' looks like father, but it is PA, a public address system; TANNOY is the British brand name used generically for one, as at railway stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Eat can mean bother or vex, as in 'what's eating you?', so it means irritate.

clue.text: Clergyman in Aran ruled out of order

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A priest on the Aran Islands has been judged to be acting improperly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean is a Church of England cleric who oversees a group of parishes.

clue.text: Eaterie serving snail, perhaps even helpings of gumbo for last couple

indicators.note: the final two letters of the mollusc word are swapped for the new ones

parts.note: a snail is an example of a gastropod mollusc

indicators.note: take the even-numbered letters, second and fourth, of the word gumbo

explanation.surface: A restaurant offers escargots and portions of gumbo for the last two diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even helpings of gumbo' takes its 2nd and 4th letters, U and B, which replace the final OD of GASTROPOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub serving high-quality food, so it is a place to dine.

clue.text: I could be slated for too sloppy parking

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are messily rearranged

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone criticised for parking far too carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slated' reads as harshly criticised, but it means covered with slates.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a house is often covered with slates, so it is something that may be slate-clad.

clue.text: Something to eat cheers weeping figure

parts.note: a pie is a food item
ta and cheers are both informal British ways to say thank you

explanation.surface: A snack raises the spirits of a tearful person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta is a sculpture or painting of the Virgin Mary mourning over the dead Christ.

clue.text: Stages empty protests in disgust? On the contrary

indicators.note: with the reversal signal, one piece goes inside the other
the surface order is flipped, so disgust holds the empty protests rather than the reverse
the word protests emptied of its middle leaves just its first and last letters

parts.note: odium is hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: Platforms for staging hollow protests in disgust, or the other way about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' tells the solver to swap the roles that 'in' suggests: the disgust word goes inside, and the emptied protests go outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Podiums are raised platforms, a kind of stage for speakers or winners.

clue.text: Door has people moving forward

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A door lets a crowd of people move ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' reads as a direction, but it is a rugby player: the loosehead prop is a front-row forward in a scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the loosehead prop packs down on the left of the front row, one of the forwards.

clue.text: Heretic and junkie just starting religious journey

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the four words is used

explanation.surface: An unbeliever and an addict are just setting out on a pilgrimage.
explanation.definitionFit: The hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca that Muslims make at least once if able.

clue.text: Handle jumbo, maybe, a girl polished off

parts.note: Vi is a short girl's name
to polish off food is to have eaten it all

explanation.surface: A girl has finished off something huge, maybe an elephant called Jumbo.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot an aircraft, such as a jumbo jet.

clue.text: Admin officer puts worker on publicity project

indicators.note: in an across clue the worker is placed on, that is after, the other pieces

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
to jut is to project or stick out
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: An office manager assigns a member of staff to a promotional campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a noun for a campaign but is the verb JUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is a military officer who handles administrative duties for a commander.

clue.text: Bore it's as well to avoid regularly

definitions.note: a verb defining a noun: the tool is the thing that bores

indicators.note: every other letter of as well is skipped, keeping alternate ones

explanation.surface: A dull person is best steered clear of on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the verb, defining a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a small pointed tool for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Stalin's kid captivating European parliament

indicators.note: the teasing word holds the European and parliament letters within it

parts.note: to kid is to tease, to josh
P is the abbreviation for parliament

explanation.surface: The Soviet dictator's child charms the European Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalin's' defines as 'Stalin's first name'; 'kid' is a verb (tease), not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet leader was called Iosif, rendered in English as his given name, so it is the dictator's forename.

clue.text: Blew card game advantage, discarding ace

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game

indicators.note: the letter for ace is thrown out of the advantage word, as a card is discarded

parts.note: a lead is an advantage over rivals
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A player threw away a winning position at cards by getting rid of an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blew' looks like 'wasted', but it is the sense of blowing a whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistled means made a shrill note by blowing through pursed lips or a whistle.
